breaking.headline: Russian missiles land in Poland as NATO calls it a grave violation
breaking.fact: Two Russian missiles and a suspected jet-powered drone came down in southeastern Poland Friday morning during a mass Russian strike on Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it a deliberate provocation timed to nearby allied exercises, and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called it a grave violation of Polish airspace. No casualties were reported.

breaking.headline: Tech rout deepens: S&P 500 falls into correction as Nvidia plunges 14%
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 slid 3.7% Friday to 6,910, entering correction territory, and the Nasdaq wiped out its 2026 gains as the AI trade unwound. Nvidia fell 14% on the day, and Anthropic dropped 8.5% a day after its record IPO debut.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed minutes make a December rate hike look near-certain
weekInBrief.body: Minutes from the Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting showed broad support for further hikes, with Governor Waller floating a 50-basis-point move in December. CME FedWatch put a quarter-point hike on Dec. 9 at roughly 90-95% odds, with a second hike eyed for January.

weekInBrief.headline: 10-year Treasury yield closes the week above 5%
weekInBrief.body: The 10-year Treasury yield finished Thursday near 5.05% and the week around 5.15% - its second trip above 5% this year - as hot October inflation and the hawkish Fed minutes repriced the path of rates higher.

weekInBrief.headline: COP31 climate summit goes into overtime in Turkey
weekInBrief.body: Delegates at the UN climate summit in Turkey failed to reach consensus on a final communique, pushing the conference into overtime amid disputes over how to tackle global warming.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump warns of a 'tremendous tax' on AI data centers built abroad
weekInBrief.body: President Trump said Friday that U.S. companies building AI data centers overseas will face a 'tremendous tax' penalty, a new pressure point for the tech giants pouring billions into AI infrastructure.

weekendStories.headline: Texans and Kroger deliver 1,000 Thanksgiving meals to Houston families
weekendStories.body: The Houston Texans and Kroger handed out 1,000 complete Thanksgiving meals - turkey and all the sides - to Houston-area families at Reliant Stadium on Nov. 10, with players and Lady Texans on hand to load bags and greet guests.

weekendStories.headline: Houston's Westside Mobile Care Day brings showers, haircuts and help to unhoused neighbors
weekendStories.body: The third Westside Mobile Care Day on Nov. 14 offered unhoused Houstonians showers, haircuts, vaccines, health screenings and help recovering IDs and birth certificates - a one-stop shop run by District F ahead of Thanksgiving.

weekendStories.headline: Superior Health Foundation gives $467,000 to 14 U.P. groups
weekendStories.body: The foundation's final 2026 grant cycle sends $467,000 to 14 Upper Peninsula organizations, including $50,000 for a small recuperative-care home in Marquette for people with nowhere safe to recover after a hospital stay.

weekendStories.headline: 10,000 acres of Keweenaw Point now open to the public
weekendStories.body: Michigan's DNR has acquired nearly 10,000 acres of forests, wetlands and culturally significant land at the tip of the Keweenaw Peninsula, now protected as public land for recreation, wildlife and future generations.

weekendStories.headline: $850,000 in grants and coaching for U.P. small businesses
weekendStories.body: A new state-funded program will deliver $850,000 in grants of up to $10,000 plus hands-on coaching to 300-400 small businesses across the Upper Peninsula, building on a first round that helped 248 businesses and is projected to create 112 jobs.

weekendStories.headline: Stockgrowers put local beef on school lunch trays
weekendStories.body: The MonDak Area Stockgrowers Association gave $3,250 to Bainville schools to buy locally produced beef for lunches - part of $48,000 the ranchers' group has provided this year to schools across eastern Montana and western North Dakota.

weekendStories.headline: 26 rescued chinchillas fly 'Chin Force One' to a new life in Florida
weekendStories.body: Twenty-six chinchillas rescued from a filthy Ohio breeding operation flew to Freeport, Florida aboard a donated private plane, where Alaqua Animal Refuge built them a new home; 12 more continued on to an adoption agency in Oklahoma.

weekendStories.headline: Four orphaned cougar cubs find their forever home
weekendStories.body: After their mother was killed in Washington, four cougar cubs - the smallest under six pounds - were rescued and made a 27-hour trip to The Wildcat Sanctuary in Minnesota, where they now have names, warm dens and a lifetime of care.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

comic.title: Plate Maintenance
comic.alt: First we're going to have to relieve the built-up strain, but we'll do it one hemisphere at a time, so you'll just need to briefly move all your fragile stuff like buildings over to the other hemisphere while we work.

space.headline: Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object one light-day from Earth
space.body: NASA's Voyager 1 crossed one light-day - about 16.1 billion miles - at 5:16 a.m. ET Wednesday, Nov. 18, after more than 49 years of travel. A radio signal now takes a full day to reach it, and NASA confirmed the milestone Thursday when the signal arrived at mission control.

space.headline: Nine-pound eagles hunt 60-pound baboons - and may have hunted our ancestors
space.body: Verreaux's eagles in Chad were found hunting full-grown olive baboons weighing up to 58 pounds, with talon punctures in skulls recovered on the Ennedi Plateau. Since early hominins weighed about the same, researchers say aerial ambushes may have shaped how our ancestors cooperated and communicated.

space.headline: Homo erectus teeth rewrite the species' story
space.body: Teeth from two caves in southern China show Homo erectus survived in mainland Asia up to 216,000 years longer than thought - as recently as 184,000 years ago - and lived in tropical rainforest, a habitat once believed only modern humans could handle.

space.headline: Rembrandt's 'Night Watch' is teeming with microbes
space.body: Researchers swabbing the 1642 masterpiece found a hidden world of bacteria on its surface, including skin and soil microbes and one puzzling species first found at a Japanese sugar refinery in 2013 - the first time any artwork has been analyzed this way.

apod.title: Voyager's Neptune
apod.credit: Voyager 2, NASA — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 21, 2026
apod.explanation: Voyager 2 made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989 - the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant. This composited scene, built from images recorded during the flyby, shows the dim planet and its largest moon Triton as thin sunlit crescents, with cirrus clouds and a dark band circling Neptune's south polar region and parts of its very faint ring system. Still cruising in 2026, Voyager 2 is now in interstellar space.
